title: Don't Repeat Yourself! Coarse-Grained Circuit Deduplication to Accelerate RTL Simulation
problem: RTL simulation is prohibitively slow for complex digital designs, and parallel simulation runs contain significant redundancy from replicated circuit components that existing simulators fail to exploit.
motivation: Accelerating RTL simulation through circuit deduplication reduces design verification time and improves productivity in complex digital hardware development.
method: RTL simulation (register-level circuit testing) is slow for complex hardware designs. The approach identifies circuit modules that appear multiple times and deduplicates them at a coarse-grained level—treating each module as a whole unit instead of examining its internal structure. Across parallel test runs, this allows identical modules to be simulated once and their results reused for all copies, rather than each copy being recalculated separately.
key_novelty: The innovation is to deduplicate replicated hardware components across parallel simulations—treating each component as a single unit (coarse-grained deduplication)—so identical components are simulated once instead of redundantly for each copy.
contributions: Identifies circuit deduplication opportunities in parallel RTL simulation workloads
Proposes coarse-grained deduplication mechanism for RTL simulators
Demonstrates significant speedup in simulation time through shared computation
Improves resource utilization of parallel simulation server farms
primary_theme: RTL simulation acceleration via circuit deduplication
